key_findings: Mice witnessing a cagemate's social defeat (OSD) show increased consolation allogrooming toward the familiar defeated partner; visual but not olfactory cues are required.
OSD selectively activates MeA GABAergic (not glutamatergic) neurons during allogrooming; ACC and BLA were not significantly activated.
OSD reduces mIPSC frequency onto MeA GABAergic neurons without changing intrinsic excitability, causing disinhibition.
NG2 glia preferentially contact gephyrin-positive inhibitory synapses on MeA GABAergic neurons and become Ca2+-quiescent during OSD.
Optogenetic inhibition or ablation of MeA NG2 glia reduces inhibitory input to GABAergic neurons and enhances allogrooming; Gad1 knockout in NG2 glia recapitulates this.
The mechanism requires elevated corticosterone induced by social defeat.
